message.content:
In Christian theology, **Jesus Christ** is regarded as the most important prophet—and indeed the most central figure of the faith. He is seen as the fulfillment of the Old‑Testament prophecies and the ultimate revelation of God’s will.  

While Jesus is the focal point, other prophets are also highly significant:

| Prophet | Role in Christianity |
|---------|----------------------|
| **Moses** | The lawgiver who delivered the Ten Commandments; he is often called the “greatest of the prophets” because he led Israel out of Egypt and received the covenant from God. |
| **Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, etc.** | Major prophets whose writings anticipate the coming of the Messiah and outline God’s plan for humanity. |
| **John the Baptist** | The forerunner who prepared the way for Jesus, calling people to repentance and baptizing them in the Jordan River. |

So while many Christians honor all of these figures, Jesus is typically viewed as the supreme prophet—he is the culmination of prophetic tradition and the one who brings the message of salvation to the world.
